summary:
Caraga records no regional-level regulation of same-sex sexual activity or of transgender identity in the sourced material, so no regional prohibition applies to a visitor beyond the national framework. The region's only documented instrument addressing sexual orientation and gender identity is a non-discrimination ordinance adopted by Butuan City, the regional capital, in 2016.

That ordinance is a city-level measure. Its coverage runs to the boundaries of Butuan City and does not extend to the rest of Caraga, whose provinces and municipalities have no equivalent instrument in the sourced material. A trans visitor staying outside Butuan City therefore has no local non-discrimination coverage to point to.
tangentialFactors: The Butuan City ordinance is the sole Caraga entry in the national tally of local SOGIE ordinances, which otherwise clusters in Luzon and the Visayas. Caraga's inclusion in that tally rests entirely on one city government's action rather than on any regional or provincial instrument.
localsOnly: Residents of Butuan City hold local non-discrimination coverage on grounds of sexual orientation and gender identity under the 2016 city ordinance. Residents elsewhere in Caraga have no comparable local instrument identified in the sourced material, leaving them dependent on whatever coverage other instruments supply.
outOfScopeNotes:
The text of the Butuan City ordinance, its protected grounds beyond sexual orientation and gender identity, its penalties and its complaint route are not set out in the sourced material. No enforcement action, complaint or tribunal decision under the ordinance is recorded.

No trans-specific violence, detention practice, health-care rule or facility policy specific to Caraga appears in the inventory. Whether the ordinance has been applied in practice, and how it treats trans residents specifically, is unresolved on the available sources.
